Approach and rationale Our approach combines structured perturbations and resolution adaptation to break through the current local optimum without relying on time-consuming phase-wise optimization sequences. Unlike the previous strategy focusing on gradient-based local searches from a fixed starting point, our method applies carefully designed modifications to explore diverse regions of the solution space more efficiently. These structured changes are designed to systematically alter the function's support and correlations while maintaining feasibility. The core innovation is to use adaptive combination of multiple perturbation strategies (sinusoidal, block, and random), being locally optimized, and dynamically adjusted through Bayesian optimization principles to maximize improvement per budget cycle. Mathematical specification The optimization problem: - Variables: Piecewise-constant function h(x) defined on 2D grid with n points, x∈[0,2] - Objective: C5 = (1/n) * maxₖ ∑ᵢ h[i] * (1 - h[i+k mod n]) (discrete approximation of overlap integral) - Constraints: - 0 ≤ h[i] ≤ 1 for all i - ∑ᵢ h[i] = n/2 - Objective evaluation: Compute cross-correlation of h and (1-h) across all shifts The algorithm maintains an active solution h and iteratively updates it using: - Project-feasible operation (clipping + scaling to meet integral constraint) - Bayesian-guided selection from four perturbation strategies: 1. Sine-perturbation: h(x) + 0.02sin(2π·f·x) 2. Block-perturbation: Systematic modification of 7-8 contiguous segments 3. Cosine-perturbation: h(x) + 0.015cos(4π·f·x) 4. Gaussian-perturbation: Addition of random noise (0, σ) Each perturbation is optimized using SLSQP while dynamically adjusting: - Constraint tightness parameters (γ₁,γ₂) - Length scale (α) of perturbation projection - Maximum iterations (mₘₐₓ) decreasing with phase Adaptive resolution handling: Solutions are maintained through interpolation/decimation on {32,64,96,128,160,192,224,256,288,320} grid sizes (2:1 ratio) Implementation guarantees: - All h are clipped to [0,1] before feasibility projection - Feasibility projection solves: min ||h-h_clip||₂ s.t. 0≤h≤1, ∑h=n/2 - Objective evaluation uses np.correlate with mode="full" and factor dx=2/n - Results are saved with n_points and true overlap score Implementation procedure Input/Output - Input: seed=42, budget_s (seconds), kwargs - Output: (h_values, c5_bound, n_points)
